description: Regional grid instability in Northern Europe is directly attributed to uncoordinated power draw from AI data centres, triggering emergency rationing and cross-border disputes over energy allocation. The crisis forces a temporary freeze on new compute deployments and accelerates calls for binding EU-level energy governance for AI infrastructure.

Widespread strikes erupt across public administration, healthcare, and legal services as mid-level professionals face accelerated displacement due to AI adoption in back-office systems. The unrest is concentrated in countries where retraining programs have collapsed under political strain, and it forces a reassessment of the pace of automation in core state functions.
